fit: black soybean seed coat extract and drowsiness during a task
assessment: Contemporaneous author summary and likely same-study patent report lower task-day VAS at two time points in healthy adults. The baseline change comparison is inconclusive. Journal full text and trial identity remain open. Exposure is Glycine max extract.

fit: randomized whole diet and daytime dysfunction in diabetes
assessment: Adjusted PSQI daytime dysfunction difference −0.41 (95% CI −1.00 to 0.18, p=.163). The diet analysis pools bean intake and measures neither black bean preparation nor Parkinson daytime sleepiness.

fit: verified boiled black common bean meals in healthy adults
assessment: Registered crossover, dissertation and journal report describe one trial with vascular and metabolic measures. Sleepiness was outside the reported endpoints.

fit: three arm soybean extract comparison and sleepiness on waking
assessment: The earliest verified patent source reports no statistically significant between-arm sleep factor differences, with 65 evaluable. It uses Glycine max extract and a waking-time measure in healthy adults. The different 2025 study design cannot establish participant independence.

fit: black soybean seed coat extract and sleepiness on rising
assessment: In 64 healthy adults randomized to extract or placebo, immediate-on-waking OSA-MA scores favored extract at weeks eight and twelve. Extract species, population and outcome differ from the frozen claim.

fit: mixed oral oils and planned adverse smell changes
assessment: First posted in 2026 after reported completion. The mixed essential oil study schedules adverse smell checks and has no posted results. The independent cinnamon effect and Parkinson olfaction remain unresolved.

fit: cinnamon used as a diagnostic smell-test stimulus
assessment: Participants identified scents including cinnamon and orange. The comparison measures existing olfactory impairment and cognition, with no cinnamon consumption measurement.

fit: cinnamon diagnostic smell cue in the 40-item UPSIT
assessment: Original Figure 4 explicitly lists cinnamon. The smell identification comparison establishes diagnostic context. Food intake was outside the study design.

fit: oral ground cinnamon and rated meal-smell pleasantness
assessment: In 19 men with diabetes, ground cinnamon and control sessions yielded inconclusive breakfast-smell pleasantness contrasts. Clinical olfaction and Parkinson disease were outside the study design.
